The answer is identical whether or not the address has an account, and whether or not the
request was throttled (legacy defect D19: the old answer revealed which addresses exist).

put.summary: Change your password (or set a first one after signing up with Google)

post.description:
Creates the account and its own workspace, signs the person in (unverified) and emails the
verification link. In the private beta an invite code is required.

One answer for every failure (unknown address, wrong password, Google-only account), and
Laravel's timebox keeps the response time the same, so the endpoint cannot tell which
addresses have accounts.

post.summary: Sign out and end the session

get.summary: The state of two-factor sign-in for this account and this session. Never the secret

post.summary: Start setting it up: a new secret, as a QR code and as text for manual entry
Finish setting it up with a first code. The recovery codes are shown only now
Prove the second factor for this session: an app code or a recovery code
New recovery codes (the old ones stop working). Needs the second factor in this session
Start a chunked upload of a feed file (up to the size cap)

put.summary:
Send one chunk as the raw request body (`application/octet-stream`). Chunks may arrive in any
order and be sent again; each must have exactly its expected length

post.summary: Complete the upload: the chunks are assembled, checked and imported

together exceed the limit.
